column1: # Frozen file-size exceptions.
# Format: path<TAB>max_lines<TAB>reason
# A record means: the file checked, its responsibility one, frozen at this size.
# Growing past a line needs a new, larger record with a new reason. Shrinking is
# allowed and wanted: a shrunk file stales the record, and the gate demands lowering
# cap — or the ratchet stops describing reality.
# Order from the agent kit (docs/project-structure.md §2): to 300 a normal target
# size, 300–500 allowed under one responsibility, 500–800 a mandatory edge review,
# past 800 only with a pinned reason and a split plan. This project starts from an
# honest debt admission, not a clean imitation: all six files below crossed the cap
# before the gate stood. Mass splitting stays out of task work (same §9), so freeze
# first, split in separate tasks.
# The server.py, test_protocol.py and composer.py caps rose once, in round 13: delivery
# and file-gate edits grew exactly these files, not new ones. The ratchet fired stopping
# the commit on a red gate — that is its job, and repeating it means moving the change
# out, never raising the cap.
# Round 14: the server.py and test_protocol.py caps rise a second time. The reason
# is no rule bypass: the Round-14 edits belong exactly to these files, because the
# pane-binding defect lives in server.py, the test in test_protocol.py. Nowhere else
# could take them.
# Round 14, third time: pane addressing by session name. Here the caps rise neither
# first nor bypassing: first came what the baseline records prescribe — analysis. All
# addressing logic (session_address, pane_ref_format, same_pane, pane_key) moved out of
# server.py into composer.py beside pane_identity, where it belongs, leaving server.py
# two short wrappers. The server.py cap grew 20 lines, nearly all comments on why no
# single tmux call could replace the address check.
# What stayed unmoved and why it records here, never wiped: the server.py split plan
# from the record below ("pairctl moves first") stands UNDONE, impossible this round:
# a 400-line split never runs beside a task (docs/project-structure.md §9), while the
# task was no pairctl one. The third straight cap rise means splitting server.py must
# happen in the NEXT task touching it — or the rule stops working, guarding nothing.
# Round 14, fourth and fifth time. First — `pairctl pane`, overriding the pane bind by
# human hand: pin_verdict plus the run_ctl branch, 147 lines in server.py. Second — the
# same work on tests, 204 lines in test_protocol.py.
# What matters here and why it records, never wiped. Both edits READ and check the
# pane state, never changing how the pane finds: address search, query check and
# permission-menu parsing still live in server.py. The file cannot shrink by them,
# nothing to move — moving means whole, and that is a split banned beside a task.
# The round honest total: the rule stopped guarding. It now DESCRIBES the size, pinning
# that the next task must split server.py into files. Further raising these two caps
# with no moving counts not as "rule work done" but as its repeal.
# Analysis ran before the record, as this file head demands, giving this: pairctl
# truly moves whole — it never imports the MCP layer — first into the next task. Second
# candidate names the supervisor: bin/pairpilot already holds 1167 lines with no split
# plan at all.
# Round 14, seventh time: the transcript sliding window and tail reading from the file
# end. Here the caps rise for the same reason under the same rule, but with a caveat
# outweighing the rise itself.
# Caveat: this item started from a wrong figure. "46 thousand tokens" is the file size
# (196 KB) divided by four. Those tokens never entered agent context: `pair_transcript`
# by default takes 40 records, near 2k. So rotation never drops 46k as the plan wrote,
# the figure fixed in plan-task4.md. What it truly fixes measured: tail reading stopped
# parsing the whole file (67.5 ms -> 0.4 ms on a 2 MB file, 169x faster, the tail byte
# same), while `pairctl log` with no `--limit` stopped pouring half a megabyte into
# the terminal.
# Growth volume: server.py +159, test_protocol.py +183. Of server.py near a third is
# comments explaining why reading runs from the end, why a default limit beats all.
# Past this rise: no new server.py functions with no moving out. The file passed 3900
# lines, and the next item (the digest) must either fit or demand splitting before
# writing.
# Round 15: the split happened, and both records that demanded rises four straight
# times dropped. Exactly what the paragraphs above prescribed: "analysis before the
# record", "the next task must split server.py". The task was exactly that, giving
# this.
# What moved and why so, not one 725-line file. `pairctl` splits by state ownership,
# edges visible by side effect:
# - `pairctl_authority.py` — only writing the round state;
# - `pairctl_panes.py` — pane addresses plus the three-state `pin_verdict` check;
# - `pairctl_read.py` — reading only, plus the human project overview;
# - `pairctl_cli.py` — command grammar and routing, 227 lines.
# One 725-line `pairctl_cli.py` would move the monolith next door, not split it: the
# same 19 commands, the same half-screen `run_ctl`, no edge over what matters. Commands
# resolve by a name dict, so adding a command never edits a long `if`.
# The dependency runs one way: the CLI depends on the server, never reversed. The
# reverse could only stand had `Store` and `PairSession` moved into a shared layer — a
# separate task, named first in the plan below.
# Tests followed sources at once, never a separate pass: four suites each launch alone
# in `scripts/verification-profile.tsv`, because a silently excluded suite reads as green.
# The shared fixture lives in `pair_test_base.py` — a fixture, not a third test file per
# source.
